reasons: No test is visible in the packet.
The capacity comparison is not built, and the docstring states that the status field records this honestly.
The final validator is not shown in this packet, so its behaviour is unverified.

terms.meaning: Adjusting a score by a small bounded amount so that a four means the same thing for every process.
The score originally given by the scoring agent, kept unchanged for audit.
A shared capability, such as document extraction, that several processes may use.
The share of a shared benefit assigned to one process, with all shares adding to one.
A recorded rule that one process or item must be finished before another can start.
A loop of prerequisites that cannot be scheduled because each waits for the next.
The number of staff in a function.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module purpose and limits
sections.what: Explains the three things only a portfolio view can see: calibration, shared enablers and sequencing. It states that this module holds no currency figures or totals.
sections.why: The docstring says the reconciler produces the map, weights and edges, while the value package does the arithmetic.
sections.watch_out: Do not add a currency or total field here. That would break the division of work.

sections.name: PrerequisiteReason
sections.title: Reasons for ordering
sections.what: Lists the five reasons one process must precede another: process order, data product, platform, capability and policy.
sections.why: The docstring says each reason needs a different remedy, so a single vague dependency would send work to the wrong team.
sections.watch_out: The docstring says these must match the mapping in another file. If one list changes, the mapping must change too.

sections.name: CalibrationAdjustment (part 1)
sections.title: Score adjustment record
sections.what: Holds one process's dimension score as written, the bounded change, the reason, the comparators and the evidence. The record cannot be changed after creation.
sections.why: The docstring says the raw score must never change, so disputes can be traced to either the scorer or the reconciler.
sections.watch_out: The adjustment is limited to a bounded range, so a large change needs a new score from the owning agent.

sections.name: CalibrationAdjustment (part 2)
sections.title: Adjusted score and its checks
sections.what: Checks that the dimension exists on the scorecard and that a process is not compared with itself. It computes the calibrated score, clamped between zero and five, and reports whether the score moved.
sections.why: The docstring says clamping is used so that a score at the top of the scale shows that no headroom is left, rather than being treated as an error.
sections.watch_out: Clamping hides how far a score was pushed beyond the scale, so the raw score must be checked when a limit seems to bind.

sections.name: EnablerAttribution (part 1)
sections.title: Shared enabler record
sections.what: Holds one shared enabler with the processes that claim it, the basis for splitting its benefit, the evidence and the weights. The record cannot be changed after creation.
sections.why: The docstring says the split must be written down so someone can disagree with it, and the total must be one so the benefit is counted once.
sections.watch_out: The enabler identifier must come from the closed list, or the enabler will not be matched across processes.

sections.name: EnablerAttribution: _check_weights
sections.title: Enabler weight and claimant checks
sections.what: Checks that weights total one within a small tolerance, none is negative, no process is listed twice, and the weights match the claimants exactly.
sections.why: The docstring says any slack in the total is a leak that double counts benefit.
sections.watch_out: The tolerance is small but not zero, so totals may differ from one by a tiny amount.

sections.name: PrerequisiteEdge
sections.title: Ordering edge between processes
sections.what: Holds one rule that a predecessor must finish before a successor, with its reason and evidence. It rejects an edge from a process to itself.
sections.why: The docstring says an edge without a reason cannot be challenged, only obeyed.
sections.watch_out: A self-edge would create an impossible schedule, so the check must remain.

sections.name: CapacityFinding
sections.title: Capacity concern
sections.what: Records a function that is asked for more work than it plausibly has, with a written concern, the affected processes and evidence. It holds no numbers.
sections.why: The docstring says the arithmetic that compares effort with headcount belongs in the value package, so the reconciler only names the concern.
sections.watch_out: The concern is a qualitative judgement and should not be read as a measured shortfall.

sections.name: ReconciliationResult (part 1)
sections.title: Whole reconciliation result
sections.what: Gathers all adjustments, enabler splits, ordering edges, cycles, capacity concerns and the capacity check status into one frozen result. The status says whether headcount was read or the check was not run.
sections.why: The docstring says an empty concern list is ambiguous without the status, since it could mean nothing was found or nothing was checked.
sections.watch_out: Cycles must be reported as a failure and not sequenced anyway, so do not drop them from this list.

sections.name: ReconciliationResult: _check_one_attribution_per_enabler
sections.title: One attribution per enabler check
sections.what: Section code was not included in the packet, so the exact behaviour is not known. By its name, it checks that each shared enabler is attributed only once across the result.
sections.why: Likely reason: it stops the same enabler being counted twice across separate attribution records. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Without the code, it is unverified whether this check runs before the result is accepted.

summary: Holds the portfolio-wide results that a single process cannot produce: adjusted scores, shared enabler splits, ordering constraints, cycles and staffing concerns.
purpose: Lets the plan see across all processes at once, so shared benefits are counted once, scores are compared fairly, and work is not scheduled before its prerequisites.
why: The docstring says a view of one process always looks clean, so reconciliation only means something across the whole portfolio.
how: First, each score adjustment keeps the raw score and records a bounded change with a reason and comparators. Second, each shared enabler records which processes claim it and how its benefit is split, with weights that must total one. Third, each ordering edge records what must come first and why. Fourth, cycles and capacity concerns are recorded as findings without arithmetic. Finally, the whole result gathers these, and a validator checks the enabler records.
inputs: Score adjustments, enabler attributions with their weights, prerequisite edges, cycles found, capacity findings and the capacity check status.
outputs: A frozen reconciliation result. Each adjustment exposes a calibrated score that stays within zero to five, and a flag showing whether it changed anything.
risks: The weight total check uses a small tolerance. The capacity status can say that headcount was read while the comparison itself does not exist yet, so an empty finding list is not evidence of no problem. The validator only checks one record, not the whole list, and the module depends on a scorecard file not shown here.
debug: If a weight error appears, check that the weights sum to one and that the keys match the claimants. If a dimension error appears, check the name against the scorecard fields. If a calibration is rejected, check that the process is not among its own comparators. If cycles are reported, the plan cannot be scheduled and must be fixed.
